note: Literature establishes SPTAN1 loss-of-function variants as causing distal hereditary motor neuropathy (dHMN11) with juvenile/young-adult onset, but emerging reports also highlight mixed neurogenic/myopathic presentations, warranting formal phenotyping.

evidence.text: Twenty patients with heterozygous loss-of-function SPTAN1 variants showed a phenotype resembling previously reported hereditary motor neuropathy cases, although deep phenotyping also identified myopathic features.

source.title: Neuromuscular disorders with evidence of both neuropathic and myopathic phenotype
source.quote: described 20 patients with heterozygous loss-of-function SPTAN1 variants showing a phenotype resembling previously reported HMN cases.

numbers.metric: patients with heterozygous loss-of-function SPTAN1 variants

evidence.text: Genes like HSPB8 and SPTAN1, which are known causes of distal hereditary motor neuropathy, can present with distal and/or axial involvement or mixed neurogenic and myogenic patterns.

source.title: Chevauchement génétique entre neuropathies et myopathies: vers une convergence des deux entités
source.quote: On the other hand, genes such as HSPB8 or SPTAN1, known to be responsible for distal motor neuropathy, have been implicated in distal and/or axial myopathy or in a mixed pattern combining neurogenic and a myogenic component
